Granted · Core EQ will try to inspect active media/game sessions. Dump formats, UID visibility and effect support vary; this is not a coverage guarantee.
Not granted · Android documents DUMP as not for third-party apps, so a grant may be refused on a stock or release build. If your TV allows it, try once from a computer with ADB:
adb shell pm grant tv.corebuilds.eq android.permission.DUMP

Checks the same release feed the other Core apps use (Latestrelease/coreeq-version.json on main). A download is offered only when the release APK matches this app\'s package, is newer than this build, and is signed by the certificate that signed it — otherwise the file is deleted and nothing is installed.
⚠ HDMI audio may carry Dolby or DTS as a bitstream here, which skips all on-device EQ, Core EQ included. To correct it, set the TV\'s Surround sound (or Audio format) to PCM.

Quality not scored · REW imports carry no SNR or decay data

Choose what you watch most. This sets how strong the optional Extra effects are (bass boost, loudness); with both off it changes nothing. Room correction is the same for every type. Auto-detect recognizes 40+ streaming apps.
Optional layers on top of room correction. All off by default; each change applies at once. Your measured correction is never changed here.
Android\'s BassBoost effect. Strength follows the Content type screen: 60% for movies, 30% general, none for news and podcasts.
Android\'s LoudnessEnhancer. Raises quiet content by up to +4 dB (podcasts, news); none for music.

+2 dB across 2.2–4.5 kHz, where most of speech intelligibility sits, back to neutral by 6.5 kHz so sibilance is not lifted. Profiles measured with the Dialogue or House target already include it, so it adds nothing there.

Ears lose bass first as volume drops (ISO 226). Switch this on at the volume you usually watch at: below it, up to +3 dB is added under 100 Hz, never below what your speaker can play. The rest of the sound is lowered to match, so nothing clips.
This output: reference %1$.0f dB, now %2$.0f dB, %3$s. Each output keeps its own reference, recorded the first time it is used; switch off and on again to record new ones.
nothing added at or above the reference
Android does not report this output\'s volume in dB (a fixed-volume output, such as a soundbar that keeps its own volume over HDMI-CEC), so there is nothing to follow and nothing is added.
Pulls loud passages down: limiter from -12 dB at 4:1. Needs the DynamicsProcessing engine; Home names the engine in use, and says when night mode cannot run.
